basis: Craniofacial/limb dysostosis; hearing loss ~60%, cleft palate >30%, persistent upper-airway obstruction in most. Eyelid shape alone does not establish ocular damage.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: upper airway is usually obstructed by micrognathia, impairing breathing. [MedlinePlus](https://medlineplus.gov/genetics/condition/nager-syndrome/)
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft palate is common (>30%) in the predominant Nager phenotype, directly affecting oral structure and feeding.

basis: Motor neuron degeneration and defining muscle wasting (80-99%); functional androgen resistance in ~86%. Diabetes and lipid disorders are minority or separate diagnoses.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: hormonal evidence of partial androgen resistance in 86%, beyond reproductive signs alone. [Endocrine study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12161529/)
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: proximal and bulbar muscle wasting is explicitly defining; skeletal muscle atrophy occurs in 80-99%.

basis: CNS and renal malformations characterize major subtypes; polydactyly estimated >30% across the spectrum. Retinal and hepatic injury vary by subtype; aggregate frequencies uncertain.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: polydactyly is common (~50-80%) in major Meckel/Bardet-Biedl phenotypes; >30% across this spectrum is an estimate, with lower penetrance in Joubert.

basis: CD3D SCID directly impairs T-cell development, with defining T-cell lymphopenia in 3/3. Infections and diarrhea do not establish additional direct organ damage.

decisions.haematologic: primary: intrinsic failure of T-cell development with lymphopenia in 3/3 is a defining blood-cell defect, alongside immunodeficiency.

basis: METTL23-related intellectual disability; pes planus in 4/4 lacks evidence of functional skeletal injury. Minor facial features and bifid uvula do not establish additional damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: pes planus in 4/4 meets frequency, but flat feet alone do not demonstrate functional damage or a clinically significant skeletal malformation.

basis: Joubert brain malformation and neurodevelopmental impairment; polydactyly in 5/5 and optic nerve hypoplasia in 2/4. Oculomotor apraxia is neurologic.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: postaxial polydactyly in 5/5 is a common structural limb malformation; it is associated involvement rather than the defining Joubert brain criterion.

basis: Mitochondrial metabolic disease with developmental impairment in 2/2; optic atrophy and neurogenic bladder each 1/2 indicate visual and urinary functional loss; very small cohort.

decisions.renal: involved: neurogenic bladder in 1/2 establishes urinary loss of function; bladder belongs to this axis, despite the neurologic cause. Frequency rests on only two patients.
decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental impairment in 2/2, with spasticity/ataxia and other neurologic deficits, establishes the core encephalopathic presentation.

basis: Bilirubin brain injury; hearing loss 30-79%; dental enamel dysplasia is a classic diagnostic tetrad component. Hemolysis is antecedent; jaundice does not establish hepatic damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: deciduous enamel dysplasia is structural dental damage and a classic diagnostic tetrad component. [Diagnostic review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20116355/)

basis: Cutis laxa with core skull/limb malformations; learning disability 3/7 (43%) and hearing impairment 3/8 (38%). Proptosis alone does not establish ocular damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: craniosynostosis (6/8), skull remodeling (8/8) and digital malformations are core syndrome features. [Original cohort](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33991472/)

basis: Definition includes neurodevelopmental disability, common nail aplasia/hypoplasia and gingival enlargement. Less frequent skeletal anomalies do not establish umbrella involvement.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: gingival enlargement is explicitly a common defining feature of this spectrum; gums belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: absent or hypoplastic nails are explicitly common defining structural abnormalities; nails belong to the dermatologic axis.
